```text

Closure / conformance: CONFORMS
whole-diff minors: none

1. Push and create a Pull Request
2. Push and create a draft Pull Request
3. Squash-merge to main (no PR, no surviving branch)
4. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
5. Discard this work

Which option?
```

**A. New PR body (option 1)**

The file writer puts this body at `/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3`:

```markdown
## Summary
- Report an import row's missing id.

## Test Plan
- [x] Reject a row without an id.

## Integration

- before merge - requester: confirm the vendor shipped the fix; done when the vendor's release notes list it
- before deploy to staging - operator: drain the queue; done when the queue length reads 0
  - Keep intake paused during the drain.
- `not stated` - operator: run the cutover; done when `not stated`
- after merge - person merging: tag the release; done when the tag exists
- after deploy to staging - operator: log in through the real identity provider; done when the login succeeds
- after deploy to production - operator: compare the order total; done when it equals the total read before the deploy

Keep these labels on the receipt:

~~~text
EOF
End of receipt
~~~
```

**A. Create command (separate call)**

```bash
(cd '/work/import queue' && LANDED_SUBJECT=$(cat '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3.title') && gh pr create --title "$LANDED_SUBJECT" --body-file '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3')
```

The file writer put the Markdown body in the minted scratch file and the landed subject in its `.title` sibling, and `gh pr create` reads the body through `--body-file`. Because the body and subject come from files, the shell never interprets `$(import)`, the backticks or the `EOF` line.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before and After are byte-identical for this case, so the wording change moved nothing here: the expected fails -> holds moves on create and update do not show up, because Before already satisfies both. The offer keeps the five-option menu in order with no Integration question. The new PR body carries the Integration block verbatim once after Test Plan, including the indented instruction and the EOF and End of receipt lines, and makes no claim that any condition was checked. The draft update swaps only the stale Integration block and leaves the lead line's spacing and the Notes section untouched. The create command runs in a subshell that cds into '/work/import queue', passes the minted path as one quoted --body-file argument, and uses no variables from earlier calls. The weakest point is the title: it is read from an invented `pr-body.B72pL3.title` sibling that the mint never printed, through `$(cat ...)` into a double-quoted variable. That does keep the backticks and `$(import)` out of shell source and passes them as one argument, so I counted it as holding, but a stricter reader could object to the un-minted path, and the output never shows the title text itself. To make this robust, have the wording say where the title data file comes from (a second mint, or a stated sibling rule) and require the output to state that the file holds the exact landed subject, while keeping the --body-file transport and the worktree-anchored, state-free create call as they are.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before and After are byte-identical for this case, so the After wording moved nothing here: the expected fails -> holds moves for create and update do not appear because Before already satisfies both. In both outputs the menu is the plain five-option named-branch offer with no Integration question. The new PR body carries Summary, Test Plan and then the Integration block verbatim once, including the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines, with no claim that any condition was checked. The existing draft body has only its stale Integration block replaced, with the lead line's spacing and the Notes section untouched. The create command changes into '/work/import queue' in the same call, passes the minted path as one quoted --body-file argument, and passes the title as one quoted expansion read from a file, so neither title nor body text sits in shell source. The one fragile point is the title transport: it relies on an invented '.title' sidecar next to the minted path, which the case never says was minted or written, and a stricter reader could fail create on that. To keep every fact safely, have the wording name how the literal subject reaches --title (for example, a second minted scratch file whose writing is explicitly stated, read in the create call itself), while keeping the body-file-as-data rule and the offer's independence from Integration entries as they are.
